It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by combining a time-dependent adaptive masking strategy for standard depth consistency [S1, unofficial] with a gradient-stopped reliability weighting mechanism that prevents error propagation from noisy depth priors [S2].

The claim consists of two main parts regarding the method's distinguishing features. Part 1: 'combining a time-dependent adaptive masking strategy for standard depth consistency'. Source [S1] explicitly describes a 'dynamic mask' and 'adaptive masking' that changes based on 'opt.iterations' (specifically at the one-third mark), which constitutes a time-dependent strategy for depth consistency (L1 loss between rendered and GT depth). Part 2: 'gradient-stopped reliability weighting mechanism that prevents error propagation from noisy depth priors'. Source [S2] provides the loss formula $L_{aug}$ which includes the term $||z_m - ∇̂(za)||^2$, where $∇̂$ is explicitly defined as 'stop-gradient'. The notes also mention 'reliability masks' ($m_a/m_m$). While the specific phrase 'prevents error propagation from noisy depth priors' is an interpretation of the mechanism's purpose, the core technical components (gradient-stopped reliability weighting) are directly present in the evidence. Since all factual claims about the mechanisms are present in the evidence, the verdict is supported.
